rationale: Round-3 audit of f72803bb (the full 246-line diff reviewed; worktree HEAD confirmed at the fix commit). BOTH of my round-2 asks are ADDRESSED, each verified against real git semantics rather than taken on the fix author's word. ASK 1 (seeded temp index): ADDRESSED — protocol step 1 now runs `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git -C wtPath read-tree <tip>` BEFORE the exclusion-bearing `add -A`, states the load-bearing rationale (empty index + exclusion = artifact ABSENT from T = synthetic deletion; seeded = unchanged-at-tip, tip blob/mode retained), and mirrors it in bead 6 step 1 and the ADR-0041 amendment description. The exact fixture I asked for lands as leg (v) (user commit's diff vs tip NEVER touches the named artifact — red against the empty-index deletion) plus a stronger leg (vii) (artifact byte-identical at tip, in T, and in the user commit; changes only in the sync commit). Mechanics re-derived: read-tree/add/write-tree all honor GIT_INDEX_FILE; the seeded exclusion leaves the tip index entry in place, so T carries the artifact and base→T shows only bead-committed artifact changes, same as today's base..beadHead range. ASK 2 (real-index transition): ADDRESSED — materialization is now a fully specified three-part op: `C = commit-tree T -p <tip>`; `update-ref refs/heads/bead/<id> C <expected-old-tip>` (the three-arg CAS form — a genuine git semantic, so a concurrent tip move fails the update with an ADR-0035 refusal and nothing advanced beyond loose objects); then `git reset --quiet --mixed` in wtPath, correctly characterized as index-only (mixed reset targets HEAD — which IS C after the update-ref — and never touches the worktree). The phantom-staged-deletion consequence and its cure are stated (and per the BRIEF were reproduced empirically), fixture (vi) asserts an unchanged-after-snapshot worktree is status-CLEAN after materialization (red against the phantom state), rewritten (iv) asserts the interval edit survives as ORDINARY UNSTAGED dirt rather than an index/HEAD split, the reset-failure leg is forward-only with an idempotent re-run recovery (consistent with ADR-0041 §2/§3's never-rollback), and my CommitPaths safety note is incorporated verbatim (pathspec-limited, gitops.go:1699). The expected-old-tip CAS operand goes BEYOND my ask and closes a concurrency hole I had not raised — a genuine improvement. Residual-dirt WARN citation: the plan says complete.go:928-933; the full block including both closing braces is :928-934, with the WARN Fprintf itself at :931-932 — the cited range covers every semantically relevant line, so this is an off-by-one on a closing brace in prose, not a grounding error. Secondary regression scan of the rest of the diff in my lens territory: chunk 2 gains internal/approve/impl.go, consistent with impl.go:277 being an EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 invocation site bead 2 must edit; G4's read-path design consumes the exported LegacyPhaseSignature lock-free at the derive.go:179-193 consistency branch (the branch exists exactly there, verified round 1) and the legacy notice's `repair phase` recovery is made self-healing by adding repair/release to the invocation sites — all buildable as described; G3's zero-callers-outside-allowlist fence at bead 1 tightened to exactly-one at bead 2 resolves the bead-1-gate satisfiability issue cleanly. One non-blocking observation on G5 (another reviewer's addressed territory, noted for the record only): the Windows takeover's post-create verify is a verify-ONCE, so a strictly-interleaved second stale contender that passed its compare-and-delete read before the winner's create can still delete the winner's verified-fresh lock afterward — 'closing the residual delete/create interleave' slightly overstates a mechanism the plan itself already scopes as best-effort within the same-machine model, with the flock path authoritative on unix; wording could say 'narrows', but this does not affect correctness of the plan's commitments or any AC. No new issues introduced by f72803bb in my lens. The plan's grounding is now sound end-to-end: every code claim I audited across three rounds re-derives true at the reviewed commit, and the two mechanism holes I found are closed by construction with red-on-revert fixtures.
